item.title: TikToker Ayesha Gilamana murder case takes shocking turn as police uncover family link
item.description: Authorities are delving into a chilling possibility of familial ties in the murder of TikTok star Ayesha Gilamana. Five people, including her father and brother, have been taken into custody amid allegations of an honour killing. Investigators have revealed technical evidence and CCTV footage that link the family to the crime. The inquiry aims to clarify the specific roles of those involved in this tragic case.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Twitch streamer Kameaisweird’s Uber ride takes unexpected turn after driver recognizes her
item.description: Twitch streamer Kameaisweird found herself in a harrowing Uber experience on August 22, 2026, as the driver made transphobic comments and insisted she stop filming. In a moment of defiance, Kamea splashed water at him before making her exit. Viewers quickly began to debate the reality of the situation and Kamea's decision to respond visibly, resulting in a vibrant dialogue on social media.

item.title: TikTok food influencer Doctor Food arrested in Lebanon over alleged drug-linked food products
item.description: Lebanese authorities arrested TikTok food influencer Georges Dib, known as Doctor Food, on August 23. He was sought for alleged drug-related crimes involving food products made by his businesses. Police had reportedly been searching for Dib for years and he was previously sentenced in absentia. Investigators believe Dib avoided capture while continuing to post videos online for his followers.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Homicide Ruling Detailed: LA examiner finds Celeste’s death was homicide; D4vd lawyers deny murder
item.description: A newly unsealed medical examiner’s report has revealed that Celeste Rivas Hernandez died from multiple penetrating injuries, with her death officially classified as a homicide. The findings add a major development to the case involving streamer D4vd, who faces a first-degree murder charge and has pleaded not guilty. His attorneys maintain his innocence, while Celeste’s family continues to seek justice following the teenager’s death and disturbing discovery of her remains.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: We Are Charlie Kirk Controversy: Hasan Piker hits back at backlash; calls Republicans “grifters”
item.description: Hasan Piker has responded to backlash over singing “We Are Charlie Kirk” during a live show, dismissing what he called repeated “fake outrage.” In a fiery stream, the Twitch commentator claimed he was more respectful toward Charlie Kirk than Erika Kirk and criticized Republicans attempting to carry Kirk’s legacy. Piker also called them “goddamn grifters,” adding fresh fuel to an already heated controversy surrounding his performance.

item.title: A businessman bought a 23,000-acre Scottish sporting estate and spent two decades rewilding it
item.description: An ambitious English businessman has reimagined a historic Scottish hunting estate as a lush wilderness reserve. His initiative, which includes the planting of over one million native trees, has revived populations of red squirrels in the glens. The project also emphasizes the restoration of peatlands and the breeding of Scottish wildcats, with funding from upscale eco-tourism driving significant conservation efforts to protect and restore local ecosystems for the future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2019, Florida began sinking mermaid-shaped reef sculptures; the project now has more than...
item.description: A remarkable endeavor has come to fruition with over 300 artistically crafted reef modules now anchored in the depths off South Florida. This seven-year journey melds art with conservation, creating artificial habitats from sustainable concrete that nurture marine species. Supported by local governments, this innovative project aims to enhance tourism while safeguarding natural ecosystems, with aspirations for international expansion in attracting marine life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A British couple bought a derelict 85-foot, seven-storey Victorian water tower at auction
item.description: In Kennington, a neglected Victorian water tower dating back to 1877 has been transformed into a stunning family residence. This Grade II-listed landmark, originally built for an asylum, underwent a lavish restoration by a British couple. They incorporated a contemporary glass cube and an additional utility tower, resulting in a remarkable home boasting four bedrooms and panoramic views of the city.

item.title: Meghan Markle's father Thomas 'hurt' as she and Harry return to UK without meeting Archie, Lilibet
item.description: Meghan Markle’s estranged father Thomas Markle says he is “hurt and upset” after learning that Meghan and Prince Harry are reportedly returning to the UK with their children, Archie and Lilibet. The 82-year-old, who has never met his grandchildren, says he fears their move will end his hopes of ever meeting them.

item.title: In 2020, Phoenix coated 36 miles of roads to fight extreme heat; surfaces became 12°F cooler at noon
item.description: Phoenix has implemented a reflective coating on its roads to mitigate urban heat island effects, effectively reducing asphalt temperatures during daylight hours. However, researchers observed that this treatment inadvertently intensified heat radiation exposure for pedestrians in close proximity. They concluded that incorporating shade from trees and buildings is essential for enhancing human comfort, suggesting cities explore a variety of solutions beyond just reflective coatings to address rising temperatures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Alaska eradicated rats from a 6,869-acre Aleutian island more than two centuries after they...
item.description: After two hundred years of invasive rat habitation, Hawadax Island witnessed a remarkable transformation. Within just two years of their removal, native bird populations surged by over 200 percent. Seabirds previously thought extinct began to return, nesting on the island's enchanting cliffs. The restoration of the island's original name, Hawadax, marks a significant ecological achievement and sets a global benchmark for invasive species management.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: World's highest-ranking penguin Sir Nils set to become a dad after partner lays egg at Edinburgh Zoo
item.description: The world’s highest-ranking penguin, Major General Sir Nils Olav III, is set to become a father after his partner Connie laid an egg at Edinburgh Zoo. The surprise arrival marks the zoo’s first king penguin egg in 17 years. Keepers are closely monitoring the inexperienced parents as they take turns protecting and warming the egg.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2021, Alabama students began placing discarded Christmas trees along dunes to trap sand
item.description: Alabama's fragile sand dunes are being restored with discarded holiday trees, as students and volunteers team up to plant native vegetation along the coast. This innovative project marries sand trapping techniques with the introduction of native plants to stabilize the dunes. This effort not only protects essential infrastructure but also fosters crucial habitats for local wildlife, showcasing an eco-friendly method for coastal restoration and habitat recovery.

item.title: Ohio mother says son's body parts were removed as 'anatomical gifts' without her consent after death
item.description: Andrea Mauk says her 18-year-old son Damon’s eyes, skin, heart valves, ligaments and other tissues were recovered as “anatomical gifts” after his fatal Ohio crash, without her knowledge. She was in Costa Rica when he died and says the hospital never contacted her. Her grief has since become a campaign for stronger family consent and notification laws.
